tips.comment: Gary and Josh Moore's 6yo Attendu gelding was a really consistent performer last term, finishing runner-up for the fourth consecutive time at Ascot in October, doing his best work at the finish. Probably a better run than the bare result would suggest given his track position when fifth at Newbury (12f, heavy) on final outing of the season and likely significant that he makes his reappearance over a mile. Big shout.
Hartswood has not been bad this year with two wins on the AW. Interestingly, he won when last here in September and could be worth a chance with the rider claiming 5 lbs.
Not a race to get over-involved, but this Fanshawe horse, although it tends to do things the hard way by missing the kick, does stay on. It will likely frame and win if away on terms.

SERENITY DREAM has won a race at 7f, sixth over 7f at Southwell on his latest outing earlier this month. He is wearing a visor for the first time today. Upped in trip to 1m should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.
Mr Jetman ran a solid race when third at Newcastle on stable debut, showing he’s well-handicapped. With conditions to suit and a strong pace to aim at, he could go close.

Calanthe won at Lingfield in September and has since run consistently, finishing in the first 4 in 7 of his last 10 starts. This is his first run on turf since his racecourse debut when he was 3rd at Leicester last July. If he can transfer his AW form to the flat, he looks a good each way bet with 6 places on offer.

Havana Prince is a 4-year-old gelding trained by Tony Coyle. Kaine Wood is 4/16 wins, so he knows how to get the job done. A winner on today's good ground three times and has won twice over today's trip. Sits just 3 lb above last winning mark on 67 and has the extremely capable Mr. Ross Birkett in the saddle, 10/73 wins, 17/73 placed in recent years. Havana Prince will strip a lot fitter today on second start after a 214-day break and should be more competitive today in this contest.
The stable is converting at 25% in March, with 6 winners from 24 runners. Bought cheaply out of Joseph O'Brien's yard. Has an each-way chance for the in-form stable.

Won on turf in 2023, his first and sole win so far. Has had some decent runner-up efforts on the AW without winning. Has shown signs that a step up to this trip could suit and has been unlucky in the past, having not had much room, etc., when trying to challenge. If getting a clear run over this trip, could be interesting.
Al Suil Eile has won on the flat , together with eight wins on the all weather.Won over this distance , under this jockey , at Southwell in March.Each way chance.
Darryl Holland seems to have his team in good order and uses Ned Sangster here. Tricky sort, but came in the race before out of the blue!

Has been running well of late on the AW, finishing second in 3 of the last 5 starts between 7f and 1 mile. Usually finishes powerfully from the back of the field and has been unlucky not to win in more than one of those races when not getting clear passages. That should not be the case on this track and could go close if adapting to this surface.

Amaysmont has kept improving and comes into this one on the back of form reading 5-4-3-2. Looks a decent each way prospect here and would be no surprise to see him going one better than that last second at Chelmsford.
Only win came on an all-weather track, but off this mark and with the ground in its favor, it can run a big race in a wide-open race.

At the odds, Addosh might be one to consider eachway. This horse runs for a yard who's horses often run well at this course so that's one positive. This horse has been showing just average form over jumps in recent races but he's possibly a better horse on the flat. Not fancied at the odds but in these races for Amateur Jockeys, anything is possible so he could be running well, the horse has the ability so if he's on a good day , he'll be running well.

Poets Dawn looks tailor-made for this race. It has a low draw and good speed figures. It will likely sit near the front but not get drawn into a fight for the lead. I think it's going to be run quick, and Poets Dawn has a STRONG each-way chance, in my opinion, at massive odds.
Won at the beginning of the season but has since found it tough at shorter trips. Could improve a pound lower and upped in trip.

The Gosden-trained Pantile Warrior has 1 win and 3 places from just 5 runs. The 3-year-old Frankel gelding got off the mark last time out in a Class 5 maiden at Chelmsford City over 1m 2f earlier this month, beating Soy Loco by 1 1/2 lengths. This is his handicap debut off a mark of 87, 1lb below Modern Utopia, rated 88. I think there is room to improve off 87, and he could prove the one they have to beat.

Big step forward on final start last season when stepped up to around this trip in a Class 2 at Newmarket, beating the odds-on favourite and well clear of the rest of the field. Scores very well across my ratings. Jack Doughty keeps the ride. Better ground probably a plus, and a four-pound rise shouldn't be enough to stop him following up.

Won his last 2 runs on heavy ground last year, but on breeding doesn't necessarily need deep ground. His dam produced several who act on top of the ground. Looks a likely improver, having literally not come off the bridle to win on his last appearance.

Chartwell Jock is a bit of a punt as he has only had three runs, but all on the AW with the latest run in January resulting in a win. He comes into this turf/handicap debut on a decent mark with Oisin Murphy and could go well.

Mersea Island is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Charlie Johnston and makes his first appearance after a gelding operation. He posted two RPRs of 78 on AW, having been beaten a short head last time out, with the third, Aegean Prince, trained by Charlie Appleby, winning next time out. He has disappointed on turf, but both runs came on soft ground, and today's good ground could bring about some improvement. Given he is a fourth foal related to three individual winners rated 78-86-99, who all won on good ground, and the dam, Meri Shika (FR), also won twice on today's good ground, we could see a big run materialize today from Mersea Island under Joe Fanning.

Maywedance comes back from a break and steps up in trip, so there’s a few unknowns with her. She showed a bit in three runs last year, especially when second at Beverley, and now makes her handicap debut off 71. Hard to know how she’ll handle the longer distance but she’s got a decent profile and the booking of Hollie Doyle is eye-catching.

With a pedigree that has produced plenty of winners, he saw the racecourse just once as a two-year-old but showed plenty of promise ahead of what could be a productive three-year-old campaign, albeit at a modest level. Finished 4th in that debut over 7f and should stay a mile.

This R M Beckett-trained colt was a well-backed favorite for his racecourse debut over seven furlongs at Wolverhampton 22 days ago but was beaten 3/4 length in second of the eight runners behind the C G Cox-trained Fearnot. With Rossa Ryan back in the saddle and improvement likely, he can go one place better today.

Race 3 at Doncaster today is the William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Novice Stakes (Class 5) for 3-year-olds over 1,414 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3yo filly Forty Years On from the George Scott yard and will be ridden by Callum Shepard. This daughter of Mayson made a sparkling debut when finishing under a length off the winner in 3rd. Normal improvement will see her as a huge contender for victory today. Must include.

Recency Bias looks sure to improve following his debut fourth placed finish over 6 furlongs at Wolverhampton. He finished well that day having looked to run a bit green. The step up to 7 furlongs sure to suit and he can run a good race today for a top stable.

Definite signs of ability in their two runs as a 2yo on the Aw @ Soutwell/Newcastle over 7f. Looks the type to make a better 3yo and very good jockey/trainer combination makes current 28/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Had an excellent time for his current yard, last season. Managed to win three times, all over 6f including over C&D in October. Off since but he's the sort to improve further and is not taken lightly on his return to action.

His mark has taken a tumble, but Dark Thirty won well when fresh last year and drops in class here but still finds himself towards the bottom of the weights. 3/5 a place with 2 wins at this level, you can forgive him plenty of his efforts last year in competitive big field handicaps. Whilst this is the same, hopefully the class drop can make a difference, whilst also being the first time he’s run over 6f in this class. He’s certainly more exposed against some less exposed, which is the biggest cause for concern, but overall there looks enough in his favour to give him a chance of hitting the places at least.

Eye Of Dubai has shown a real liking for Doncaster, bagging a win over this course and distance last November. He’s generally consistent, hitting the frame in 8 of his 12 starts, and seems to enjoy softer ground. Coming back from a bit of a break, but if he’s ready to roll, his track record suggests he could be right in the mix again.
Knebworth won this last year when second up after a break. And guess what? He comes into this second up after a break and is worth another chance even though a bit heavier than I would like.

This is the first time ever that the excellent Pam Sly has booked Oisin Murphy and this one could go very well for her on debut for the stable. There's no doubt that this Kingman gelding has the form in the book to go very close here if fit enough, and the trainer has her string in good order at the moment. The horse has been placed off 91 twice in his 3 runs in this class and is down to 86 now so the 5yos chance is there for everyone to see with conditions to suit.

Make this horse my Nap of the day here. This horse loves big field handicaps and ran well when 4th in the Ayr Gold Cup. It has since switched stables and had a respectable 3rd pipe opener on the all-weather last time. Always thereabouts and looks a good each-way bet here.
C&D winner and twice placed in this race, including runner-up last year. Handles soft ground well and can go close again if getting a strong pace to aim at.
Won first time up last season and goes on any ground. Won on penultimate start and goes well on these straight sprint tracks. Should be in the money.

Finished last season in tremendous form and looked as if still has improvement to come, especially in a big field sprint. Was fourth in an ultra competitive handicap on final start and off the same mark here can go well and though Dale Swift replaces the very decent claimer Alex Jary he has won on my fancy here at Doncaster in the past. Actually goes well here and was second over C&D last September beaten a head by an improving 3yo then in Aramram, and looks on a fair mark to me. Was beaten a short head on seasonal debut last year so can go well fresh too. Goes on any ground, acts in big fields, looks as if still progressive and stays a bit further too so if getting a strong pace here looks a cracking each way punt today.
Probe, after a four hundred and forty-four day break, had a nice run back 6/10 on the all-weather. It will be all the better for the run. Worth an each-way bet with six places!
Lightly raced and seems to flit from one stable to another. However, is feasibly well treated if on song and won first time up last season.

Does have topweight here, but not out of this off current mark of 95. Lack of recent run should not be an issue as they have run well fresh in the past, solid draw today, good jockey back up and very shrewd trainer's niche has always been the sprinting game, making current 25/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Chairmanoftheboard is a seasoned campaigner with a fair bit of experience under his belt. He’s had his moments, picking up wins here and there, and has shown he can handle different tracks and conditions. His form can be a bit in and out, but on his day, he’s more than capable of putting in a strong performance. If he turns up in the right mood, he could be involved at the business end of the race.
Havana Pusey reached the frame in four of her eight races last season and has attracted some market support overnight, in to 20/1 from 40's on Paddy Power.

This filly had two wins in a row in France last year, both over today's distance of six furlongs. Has been out of form on the last couple of occasions, but having moved to Tracy Waggott's yard since, could see some improvement at a big each-way price here.

This M Botti-trained 4-year-old gelding is the winner of three races from one mile to one mile three furlongs on good to soft ground and on the all-weather. After running on strongly in the closing stages to only be beaten a neck behind the M Appleby-trained Penzance over one mile two furlongs at Chelmsford City 17 days ago, and with that run under his belt, he looks sure to run a big race under Rossa Ryan.

Was beaten less than a length on his reappearance run last season and improved virtually every time he ran thereafter. Comes here from the same mark as he ended last season, and it seems unlikely that he has stopped improving.

George Boughey has started the season strongly, with three winners already and several others running well in defeat. His only runner on the card, Fouroneohfever, appears to go best when fresh, as shown by his hat-trick of wins on reappearance last year. Of course, he was well handicapped then and improved for the step up in trip, showing plenty of ability despite racing keenly. He was well in command twice at Chester, and a bigger field with a stronger early pace could help him settle better this time. Billy Loughnane should be able to secure a good early position from stall 2, and I can see him running well off this mark. At around 10/1, he looks the type to grab a place with bookies paying five places.

Won a hot class 2 handicap over todays distance @ Yarmouth last season and ran very well on final start over today's C/D in a class 2. Retains a decent mark of 88 today, has run very well fresh in the past, good jockey who was on board for above win back up and shrewd upcoming trainer 23 percent with a Lsp of 18.33 on his 4yo's here last 5 seasons, making current 10/1 very good Ew value in the race.

Race 5 at Doncaster today is the Weekend Winners On Sky Sports Racing Handicap (Class 3) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 2,051 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 5-year-old gelding Asgards Captain from the Dylan Cunha yard and will be ridden by Ray Dawson. This son of Make Believe is a useful individual with 7 wins from 28 starts, is holding form rather well, and is a dangerous runner in this field.

11lb higher than when winning this last season on first start from nearly 2 years off and 9lb higher than when bolting up at Chester on penultimate start last season will make life difficult but this horse is classy at best and worth a dart at here. Yard been in cracking form on the all weather in the past fortnight with two winners and five seconds from 13 runners and couple of those was done in head bobbers on the line. Beat Stressfree in this last year and though a few pounds worse off for that length and a half win is too big a price to ignore. Should run a big race and worth an each way poke.

Proven performer over this trip on softer ground, previously placed in strong handicaps. Struggled in Bahrain on quicker surfaces but could bounce back with conditions now in his favour. Interesting contender.

If you hang your hat on KINGS CODE's run in a big field at York at the beginning of last season (from a pound higher in the weights) and combine it with the improved run last time out. There's a chance he'll get involved if continuing to progress. Looks a fairly consistent sort with 9 wins and 7 places from a total of 36 runs.

The Roger Fell trained Cockalorum has a good record over this distance with six wins and eleven places. Has won in this class previously and can vie for a place in this one at rewarding each way odds.

Small eachway tip for Baryshnikov who is today's NAP selection. It's his first run back from a rest but he's a horse with ability who could be running well, last year he had some of the most consistent form of all these. He has plenty of good form in the book on similar ground conditions as to today's and the distance is ideal. It's a good race this but he's a horse with ability, could be running well, eachway. Extra places available eachway.

Crimson Road has changed stables since the end of last season, and on the face of it seems to have traded down to a smaller and less fashionable yard. Whether there's something we're not aware of for the switch it's not possible to know, and we'll only find out as the season progresses. Interesting to note that Rab Havlin, who's ridden the horse most times, has been booked to ride. The new trainer, Susan Corbett, has been in fine form lately, and I could see this one running to a place at a very big price.

Metaverse has been knocking on the door and finally got his head in front at Newmarket over 7f. He’d gone close a couple of times before that too, so the form’s solid and with Oisin Murphy booked, that’s a bit of a bonus. If he keeps going the way he has been, he’s got every chance of going close.
The favorite for this race and its form does stand out over the 7 furlongs. It has proved itself on various sorts of going, and that swayed the difficult decision. It should make the frame at least.

Back from Bahrain, where he ran in some very competitive races, YANTARNI is of interest here back over this trip. Proved potent over seven furlongs when rattling off a hat-trick over the distance last season. Comes into this a pound lighter than the last of those wins and down in grade, as well as returning to the preferred distance. If there's no adverse reaction to the endeavors in the Middle East, there's a lot to like here and he's certainly one to keep tabs on.
Won twice over this distance last year. Yet to make an impression this year when ran on the all-weather, but back on the turf and only 1 lb above his last winning mark.

OUTRUN THE STORM has won seven races from 6f to 7f. Third over 7f at Newcastle on his latest outing earlier this month. Course distance and going should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.

Under The Twilight knows how to win over 7f and usually goes well fresh, which makes her pretty interesting here. She’s a few pounds lower than when winning on her comeback last season, so she’s definitely not badly treated. If she’s fit and ready after the break, she could run a big race at a nice price. Wouldn’t be a shock at all if she hits the frame or better.

Didn't work out for Varian and the Sheikh, even after being gelded. Loughnane could have a bargain here, having paid 38k for him. He has obviously had issues, but when he ran off 91 last May, he looked well ahead of that mark and shaped much better than the bare result. Only ran one more time before connections shipped him off. Worth small each-way consideration.
The Ruth Carr trained Woodstock has proven to go well fresh in the past and this three times class winner can give a good account here in a wide open race.
Has visited Doncaster twice on decent ground and has finished 2nd over this trip and last year won over a mile from 1lb lower. Looks a cracking each way price and should be strong at the finish.
French import. Four UK runs for the 4yo last year, a couple of decent efforts in higher grade handicaps than this one. Three AW runs last month will have him fit. On an attractive mark.

Imperial Guard has been a consistent performer, often finishing in the frame over 6 furlongs. He secured a win at Kempton and has placed multiple times, including a second at Newmarket. Now stepping up to 7 furlongs at Doncaster, this longer trip could suit him well. If he handles the distance, he’s got a solid chance of being right in the mix.
Zip is a standing dish at Doncaster, having won here four times and is admirably consistent. So even though it would prefer softer ground, it can still go close here.

Tropez Power has the profile of a horse who can go well fresh and has some solid handicapping form to work from. He’s been competitive in stronger races than this and has won off higher marks, so he’s certainly not out of place in this field. Has gone well at big tracks like Ascot and Doncaster before, and if he gets a decent pace to chase and finds cover early, he’s got the tools to finish strongly.
This one has had a wind operation since its last run, as they are stepping it back up to 7f with a good jockey booking/change. A good value each way bet for the 4 places available.

Has won around here three times including twice over C&D and did so on seasonal reappearance last April but has had a pipe opener this season on the all-weather when just touched off a nose, so cobwebs have been well and truly blown off. Young claimer keeps the ride and the 5lb he knocks off is the 5lb higher mark my fancy runs off compared to last season's reappearance. Fair draw here and looks to have a great chance to my eye given likes the track and is on a fair mark. Might prefer more juice in the ground but does handle decent going and is still quite lightly raced for age. Showed on seasonal reappearance that could be one to follow this year as pulled clear of the third and could still be in the upgrade. Was just behind Archduke Ferdinanand here in September and hoping that one gives the form an even more solid look by the time this one goes in the stalls. Big shout to my eye and looks a cracking punt.

LIAMARTY DREAMER has won six races from 7f to 1m. Eleventh over 7f at Southwell on his latest outing last month. Course distance and going should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.

The trainer has had the horse for 3 runs now, having got him from the John Gosden yard. It's no surprise that he's now adding the blinkers to the usual tongue tie since the horse has been racing too keenly. The blinkers could be exactly what is required to help him settle. There's some form from when he was trained by Gosden, which would suggest he's racing off a very winnable mark here. The beating of Leadman, for example, when giving him 7lb in a novice race is certainly strong form. That horse won off, in effect, an 11lb higher mark than DC races off here by winning his next race as an odds-on favorite. DC is very lightly raced for a 5-year-old and should still be improving.

Clearly does not visit the winners enclosure as much as they should, but is normally on the premises in this grade and is not badly handicapped here off current mark of 79. Has run well fresh in the past so lack of recent run should not be an issue and good jockey/trainer combination makes current 18/1 decent Ew value here.
Stockpyle looked very stuffy on return, but with that behind, it now looks like one to have a prod at here off 73 with the tongue strap on.
Jenni has dropped to one pound above her last winning mark and has potential to go well here on first run for the Seb Spencer yard.

Glory Hyde is a speedy filly who knows how to get involved over the minimum trip. She grabbed a win at Beverley last summer and has hit the frame a few times since, so she’s clearly got a bit of consistency about her. Loves a sharp five and with a decent run through, she wouldn’t be a surprise winner in a race like this.

Was a touched off just a head and a neck on last two seaosonal reappearances so can go well fresh and looks on a fair mark here. Is 4lb lower than course and distance win last July and looks to have a lot of ticks in his box today. Speedy sort who won't mind if the ground dries out further and looks sure to get a strong pace to aim at in this and can rattle home to hit the frame at the very least.

Won a decent class 3 handicap @ Chester Festival last season off a 2lb higher mark, so would have to be considered well handicapped here in this class 5. Has run very well fresh in the past and good jockey/trainer combination makes current 16/1 solid Ew value here.

Glory Fighter is another who has raced quite recently which may be an advantage, he may be that bit more sharper than a few of today's opponents. Ran well on the AW last time out, turf probably suits this horse better so it wouldn't be a surprise to see him run well. Wide draw is a slight worry though.

Small eachway tip for Bear Rock. In yesterday's races at Doncaster, horses who had , had a recent run were doing better , Bear Rock ticks that box so he's one to consider. Improvement is needed but he's much less exposed than many of today's opponent so he may well have a bit more to offer this season.

Wicked Thoughts has won a NH flat race at 2m. Also won a point-to-point race. Second in a hurdle race over 3m 1f at Kempton on his latest outing last month. Dropped in trip to 2m 3f should suit and could well be able to go one better and win this race.
Looks like an unexposed horse that made a good start in handicap races when coming in first last time out. Up 7lb, but plenty more to come.

It remains to be seen if Torrent is well-handicapped, but he brings the best form into the race and looks the each-way pick at 11/2. He has been competing at Grade 2 level, finishing third twice behind East India Dock, often given too much to do and ridden to hit the frame rather than challenge for the win. A Newton Abbot winner in September, he then bumped into Liam Swagger, who went on to finish third in the Fred Winter, running respectably at Market Rasen and Wetherby. With winning form on quick ground, the drop into calmer waters should suit, making him a solid contender.
Moore's stable does well with runners here, and this comes here in good form. Has won and finished second in several races. Should go well.

SAUVIGNON has won two hurdle races at 2m 1f. He was fourth in a Group 2 hurdle race over 2m at Kempton on his latest outing last month. The course, distance, and going should suit. He seems well treated, dropped in class, and could well be able to win this race.

Tough to get away from Kotmask here, who has run some really sound races at this venue this season. This race looks a touch easier than most he has encountered this season. Should take all the beating here.
Third Time Lucki is down in grade and in the weight here at Ascot. With Jonathan Burke onboard, looks the likely winner and is trading at a good each way price of 100/30. Our NAP.
Hypotenus has shown signs of recent form, so he's likely to feature prominently in the race. He seems the more consistent and reliable contender, given his improving form and favorable handicap.

Coastguard Station ran here following a 99-day break last year and was not beaten far into 2nd. The three-time chase winner is much better over fences than hurdles, and his last run was over hurdles and can largely be ignored. Comes back fresh again after a 120-day break. Will need to be at his best to win, but with all rivals beaten more than 30 lengths or pulled up on their last runs, he looks too big a price to ignore.

This will be the ninth run over hurdles for NATIVE MOON. Since his move to the Jeremy Scott yard, this seven year old has picked up place money on all four starts. His second over 2m7f (Good (Good to Soft in places) at Exeter last time out was particularly encouraging. He finished second by a length and a half to a well handicapped sort. The third and fourth that day have since gone and won next time out. The handicapper has raised him 3lbs for his most recent effort but this trainer appears to have found the key to this runner and a win should be around the corner.

Up in grade and will need a career-best to win this, but he comes here in top form, going for the hat trick. Ground conditions will suit, and for a 10-year-old, he is relatively lightly raced. Should go close.

Credo has shown strong staying power, winning two of her past three outings, including a recent victory at Carlisle. Jockey Harry Cobden has developed a successful partnership with Credo. Trainer Anthony Honeyball has a solid reputation with staying chasers. Ground conditions at Ascot are not specified, but the forecasted Good to Soft should be favorable.

Sits 2 lbs below the mark he ran off in this race last season. Coming into this race with a bit to prove at present. He's evidently not as good as he once was. To be fair, he's almost a teenager now, so it's to be expected. He ran a cracker in this event last season. Beaten just 1/2 L behind the winner Sam Brown. A solid effort trying to give 8 lbs in weight to the winner. I felt he ran a great race over CD on reappearance this season behind stablemate Chianti Classico. Beaten just 7 L back in 4th place. This is clearly his favourite track. He boasts plenty of useful form here, including a 2nd place finish behind Fakir d'Oudairies in the 2022 running of the Betfair Chase. He goes well fresh, which bodes well. He can go well on good or soft ground, so the weather won't stop him. If he runs his usual race, that would see him thereabouts in this very winnable race.

Smart Chaser for Willie Mullins. Not been at the level since joining this yard, but signs that ability is intact. Although poor the last twice, the fitting of blinkers may stimulate a revival for a yard in form.

DEISE ABA has won a hurdle race, five chases, and a point-to-point race from 2m 3f to 3m. Tenth in a chase over 3m at Kempton on his latest outing in December last year. Course, distance, and going should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.
